theater: 美索不達米亞巴比倫城

battle.name: 巴比倫戰爭
battle.theater: 美索不達米亞巴比倫城
battle.brief: 前311年，安提柯自西方壓向巴比倫，圍城數月；塞琉古一世從東方回師，連夜襲營、焚毀攻城器械，反過來把安提柯困在沼澤堡壘，逼他棄城南走。這場亞歷山大遺產之爭裡沒有正面會戰，勝負全在封河、合圍與夜襲之間。卡面斯巴達長矛就是方陣手中的那一支長槍，槍尾銅套插地時，隊形才站得住。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 前311年的巴比倫戰爭，是亞歷山大大帝死後「繼承者戰爭」中爭奪巴比倫行省的一場對峙，交戰的並非兩個國家，而是兩位亞歷山大舊將的聯盟。安提柯一世獨眼（Antigonus I Monophthalmus）一方，以安提柯與其子德美特里一世圍城者為核心，握有呂基亞、卡帕多細亞等亞洲行省與地中海東岸的資源，麾下是馬其頓老兵、希臘傭兵、亞細亞徵召兵，以及一支規模可觀的攻城器械隊。塞琉古一世尼卡托（Seleucus I Nicator）一方，兵源來自他在東方淪落時重建的地區軍隊：巴克特里亞、索吉亞那與阿里奧斯達、帕提亞、大夏一帶的騎兵與步兵，另有巴比倫城內不願接受安提柯節制的一方。巴比倫城本身並非中立城市，城中有反對安提柯的守備與民間武裝，城外則是安提柯的封鎖營盤。亞美尼亞、波斯與中亞部眾多以受雇兵身分加入塞琉古的東方軍隊；德美特里在圍城後期調來的船隊，是安提柯一方唯一能從水路施壓的另一種力量。
countriesEn: The Babylonian War of 311 BC was a contest for the satrapy of Babylon inside the Wars of the Diadochi that followed the death of Alexander the Great, and the belligerents were not two states but the coalitions of two of Alexander's old generals. On one side stood Antigonus I Monophthalmus, the core being Antigonus himself together with his son Demetrius I Poliorcetes, who held the Asian satrapies such as Lycia and Cappadocia and the revenue of the eastern Mediterranean coast. Under them fought Macedonian veterans, Greek mercenaries, levies drawn from Asia Minor, and a siege train of considerable size. On the other side stood Seleucus I Nicator, whose troops came from the regional armies he rebuilt while exiled in the east: cavalry and infantry from Bactria, Sogdiana and Aria, Parthia and Hyrcania, joined by a faction inside Babylon that was unwilling to accept Antigonus's authority. Babylon itself was not a neutral city; within the walls sat defenders and armed bands hostile to Antigonus, while outside stood his cordon and blockading camps. Peoples from Armenia, Persia and Central Asia entered Seleucus's eastern army mostly as hired mercenaries, and the fleet Demetrius brought north during the later phase of the siege was the only other kind of force Antigonus could still apply, by river and by sea.
people: 安提柯一世獨眼是這場戰爭的推動者，也是亞歷山大舊部中最有野心的一位；前312年他在加薩擊敗塞琉古之後，一度把亞洲行省與巴比倫的稅收攬入掌中，隨即把矛頭指向富庶的巴比倫行省。他的兒子德美特里一世帶海軍北上，沿幼發拉底河口與波斯灣水道逼近，試圖以水上封鎖配合陸上圍城。塞琉古一世尼卡托是這場戰爭的另一主角：前319年被迫離開巴比倫後，他在東方藉歐麥尼斯的參謀逐步重建軍隊，前318年與前316年先後在帕拉塔刻涅、加比涅兩戰中擊敗歐麥尼斯的遠征軍；前312年加薩之敗幾乎讓他全軍覆沒，他靠著少數隨從逃出，數年後捲土重來。巴比倫城內另有另一股勢力：祭司階層與「全民」首領漢諾自前320年起就利用馬其頓人的內鬥反抗新來的統治者，安提柯入城後的反對派清算更使城內怨憤未消。安提柯最後決定放棄圍城、率殘部撤回波斯方向，在他自己的算盤裡，巴比倫的稅收再厚，也不值得用一支耗盡的軍隊去換。卡面那支斯巴達長矛屬於同一套戰術世界：它是方陣步兵手中的長槍，決定了一列盾牌是站住還是散開。
peopleEn: Antigonus I Monophthalmus was the man who drove this war and the most ambitious of Alexander's former generals. After defeating Seleucus at Gaza in 312 BC he gathered the Asian satrapies and the tax income of Babylon into his own hands, and he turned at once on the rich satrapy of Babylon itself. His son Demetrius I brought a fleet north, working up the mouth of the Euphrates and the waterways of the Persian Gulf, trying to combine a blockade by water with the siege on land. Seleucus I Nicator was the other protagonist of the war. Forced out of Babylon in 319 BC, he rebuilt an army in the east with the counsel of Eumenes, and in 318 and 316 BC he beat Eumenes's expeditionary force at Paraitakene and again at Gabiene. The defeat at Gaza in 312 BC had very nearly annihilated him; he escaped with a few followers and came back within a few years. Inside Babylon a third force was at work: the priestly hierarchy and Hanno the Great, leader of the Babylonians as a political body, had been exploiting the quarrels among the Macedonians to rise against the new rulers since 320 BC, and the purge Antigonus carried out after entering the city left the resentment unhealed. When Antigonus finally chose to abandon the siege and drag his survivors back towards Persia, his own reckoning was that the revenue of Babylon was not worth spending an exhausted army on. The Spartan dory on the card belonged to the same tactical world as these men: a long spear carried by the foot soldiers of the phalanx, the weapon that decided whether a line of shields held its ground or came apart.
kits: 卡面那支斯巴達長矛（Dory）並未隨軍出現在巴比倫的牆頭，卻是理解兩軍重裝步兵的關鍵：一支約兩米上下的木槍，槍首是葉形鐵刃，槍尾套著銅錐，可以插地支撐，正是希臘長柄兵器的標準形制。安提柯與塞琉古的步兵主體是希臘方陣與馬其頓式的長槍方陣，長矛從圓盾或小圓盾之後伸出，槍尖越過前排肩頭：第一排跪地，第二排挺槍，其後各排把手裡的槍搭上前排的槍身，層層疊加的槍鋒把進攻正面變成一堵不能硬闖的牆。圍城時，長矛改作守城用的長柄兵器，用來在城頭分隔登上雲梯的敵兵，或在缺口前頂住撲上來的攻城塔。真正左右戰局的還有攻城器械：可推到城牆下的攻城塔、對準門扉反覆撞擊的撞錘、拋射石塊與鐵球的配重投石機，以及用來燒毀敵方器械與營帳的火矢。軍中另有象——塞琉古在東方確實握有象兵，牠們多來自印度方向的戰利品與交易，但巴比倫一役中象的實際作用，現存記載幾乎不提。糧秣、箭矢與攻城重器材則靠幼發拉底河與底格里斯河的舟船輸送，車隊沿河岸隨行。
kitsEn: The Spartan dory on the card (Dory) never stood on the walls of Babylon, yet it is the key to reading the heavy infantry of both sides. It was a wooden shaft some two metres long, with an iron leaf-shaped head and a bronze butt-spike that could be planted in the ground to steady the push, and it was the standard form of the Greek long-handled weapon. The infantry core of Antigonus and of Seleucus consisted of Greek hoplite phalanxes and of the Macedonian-style long pike phalanx, and the framework of both was a row of long-hafted weapons of exactly that family: the spear projected past the round or small round shield, its point reaching over the shoulder of the man in front, the first rank kneeling, the second levelling its shafts, the ranks behind laying their shafts onto those ahead until the points overlapped into a wall that could not simply be walked into. Under siege the same spears changed jobs, becoming long-handled tools of the defence, used on the wall to separate the enemy coming up the ladders, or to hold a breach against the enemy assault from the siege tower. What really decided the campaign were the siege engines: towers that could be rolled up to the wall, rams that struck the gates again and again, counterweight throwers hurling stones and iron balls, and fire arrows for burning the enemy's engines and tents. The armies also had elephants; Seleucus certainly held elephants in the east, mostly taken as booty or bought through the Indian trade, but the surviving record says almost nothing about what elephants did at Babylon. Food, arrows and heavy siege stores moved on the boats of the Euphrates and the Tigris, with wagon trains following the river banks.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術主軸是圍城與反圍城，野戰反而是例外。安提柯的步驟是先封河、再合圍：他以騎兵與步兵切斷幼發拉底河兩岸的渡口與陸路，把城與外部的往來切斷，再把攻城器械一批一批運到城頭覆蓋不到的位置，一段一段夯土築壘，把壕溝填平。塞琉古的反擊完全依靠機動，他不與安提柯爭奪攻城器械，而是率方陣與騎兵晝夜兼程由東向西切入，直取營盤。夜間襲擊中，進攻方以方陣的長矛正面頂開缺口，縱火兵同時點燃安提柯的攻城塔與輜重營帳，把數月攻城所得在幾個時辰內燒成灰燼。安提柯退入沼澤地帶的堡壘，塞琉古反過來合圍，卻無法攻破，戰局就這樣僵持到冬季與翌年。德美特里的船隊在河口遭遇風浪而折損，無法接應陸上。安提柯於是趁隙突圍，僅帶少數人遁入波斯與帕提亞方向，圍城工事最終自行瓦解。塞琉古則以解放者的姿態接管城防與行省。
tacticsEn: The tactical axis of this war was siege and counter-siege; open battle was the exception. Antigonus's method was to close the river first and then close the ring: cavalry and infantry cut the crossings of the Euphrates and the land roads so that nothing passed any more between the city and the outside, and the siege engines were moved up in stages to positions the defenders on the wall could not cover, earth and rubble being packed down ramp by ramp until the ditch was filled level. Seleucus's reply rested entirely on movement. He did not fight Antigonus for the siege engines; he marched day and night with phalanx and cavalry and cut straight at the camp. In the night assault the attackers opened a gap with the points of the phalanx while the fire teams set light to Antigonus's towers and baggage tents, and months of siege work were burned down within a few hours. Antigonus withdrew into a fort in the marshes, and Seleucus turned the tables and besieged him in turn, but could not take it, and the deadlock held through the winter and into the following year. Demetrius's fleet was damaged by weather at the river mouth and could no longer support the army on land. Antigonus used the opening to break out with a handful of men and take refuge towards Persia and Parthia, and the siege works came apart on their own. Seleucus entered the city as the deliverer of the east and took over the defences and the satrapy.
data: 可核的數字不多，且多來自孤本式的轉述。巴比倫城牆的長度是現代考古測量：內城牆周長約八公里，外城牆約十八公里，全城分踞幼發拉底河兩岸，佔地約五百至六百公頃，古典時代的人口估計在數萬至十萬之間。安提柯的圍城自前311年入秋起，前後拖到翌年，歷時數月，而巴比倫是美索不達米亞最重要的產糧與徵稅之地。塞琉古在東方重建的軍隊，狄奧多羅斯（Diodorus Siculus）第十九卷記為步兵約兩萬、騎兵數千，另有少量象，各家推算略有出入；從巴克特里亞到巴比倫的陸路行程超過一千五百公里，縱隊行軍需要數月。德美特里的船隊在一次風浪中折損，記載沒有留下數目。加薩之戰前312年，塞琉古一軍的損失近於全軍覆沒，這一點各條記載一致。攻城器械的數量、守軍的編制與陣亡人數，現存史料都沒有留下可信的統計，寫下來只能是推測。
dataEn: The verifiable numbers are few, and most survive only as isolated figures in a single narrative tradition. The circuit of Babylon's walls is a modern archaeological measurement: the inner wall about eight kilometres, the outer wall about eighteen, the city astride both banks of the Euphrates and covering roughly five hundred to six hundred hectares, with a population of the classical period estimated in the tens of thousands up to a hundred thousand. Antigonus's siege began in the autumn of 311 BC and dragged on into the following year for a period of months, the city being the most important grain-producing and tax-collecting centre of Mesopotamia. The army Seleucus rebuilt in the east is given by Diodorus Siculus in the nineteenth book as about twenty thousand foot and several thousand horse, with a few elephants, estimates varying slightly from one writer to another; the land route from Bactria to Babylon runs for more than a thousand and five hundred kilometres, so a column on the march needed months of travel. Demetrius's fleet was broken up in a storm, and no figures survive for it. The losses Seleucus suffered at Gaza in 312 BC were close to annihilation, and on that point every source agrees. The number of siege engines, the establishment of the garrison and the casualty figures leave no trustworthy statistics at all, and anything written down about them would be guesswork.
cause: 起因不是某一條盟約被撕毀，而是亞歷山大大帝遺產分配本身的模糊。前323年大流士三世戰死後不到兩周，大帝在巴比倫病逝；帝國隨即在巴比倫與蘇薩召開的會議上被切成若干行省，巴比倫行省因為糧食、稅收與地理位置，一度歸於塞琉古名下，前319年塞琉古失勢出逃東方，行省又由攝政培松與安提柯重新分配。前312年加薩一役，塞琉古再次被逐出亞洲，安提柯在蘇薩召開的軍人集會上取得美索不達米亞與巴克特里亞一帶的統治權，於是「巴比倫屬誰」成為兩人無法迴避的問題：巴比倫控制著東方的糧道與錢糧，塞琉古在東方重建的每一分實力，最終都要靠這座城市兌現。安提柯的兵鋒指向巴比倫，塞琉古自東方回師，本來就是同一條線上的兩股力量。
causeEn: The cause was not the breaking of some sworn agreement but the vagueness of the partition of Alexander's inheritance itself. Less than two weeks after the death of Darius III, the Great King fell ill and died at Babylon; the empire was then cut into satrapies at the conferences held at Babylon and at Susa, and the satrapy of Babylon, with its grain, its taxes and its position on the map, fell for a time to Seleucus. When Seleucus lost his footing and fled east in 319 BC, the regent and Antigonus redistributed it once more. After Gaza in 312 BC threw Seleucus out of Asia a second time, Antigonus took the rule of Mesopotamia and the lands towards Bactria at the soldiers' assembly held at Susa, and the question of who owned Babylon became one the two of them could no longer avoid: Babylon commanded the grain routes and the money of the east, and every soldier Seleucus raised in the east ultimately had to be paid for out of that city. Antigonus's advance towards Babylon and Seleucus's march back from the east were simply the two ends of the same line.
impact: 巴比倫落入塞琉古手中，成為塞琉古王朝的根基。此後亞歷山大的帝國在東西兩線分家：安提柯系佔有地中海東岸與小亞細亞，塞琉古系佔有從美索不達米亞到中亞的內陸。巴比倫帶來的稅收，讓塞琉古能夠養出常備軍與龐大傭兵隊，也讓他有能力在前301年伊普索斯會戰擊敗安提柯與德美特里。以君主之名命名的希臘式新城模式由此確立：方格街道、圍牆與護城河，塞琉古把重心放在底格里斯河畔的塞琉古城（Selucia on the Tigris，一般認為始建於前311年前後），巴比倫則退居其次。希臘語在美索不達米亞成為官方與商業語言，希臘式的長矛方陣也隨著軍隊與移民進入兩河平原，成為此後數百年希臘化東方的骨架。而東亞與中亞的門戶一旦敞開，希臘化世界與帕提亞、巴克特里亞乃至更遠的印度之間的商路與使節往來，隨之連成一片。
impactEn: Babylon in the hands of Seleucus became the foundation of the Seleucid state. The empire of Alexander was thereafter divided along a west-east line: the Antigonids held the eastern Mediterranean and Asia Minor, the Seleucids held the interior from Mesopotamia to Central Asia. The taxes of Babylon allowed Seleucus to maintain a standing army and enormous numbers of mercenaries, and to beat Antigonus and Demetrius at Ipsus in 301 BC. The pattern of the Alexandrian city was thereby established, a city named for its ruler and laid out on a Greek grid of streets with walls and a moat, and Seleucus placed his centre of gravity in Seleucia on the Tigris, generally held to have been founded about 311 BC, with Babylon demoted to second place. Greek became the official and commercial language of Mesopotamia, and the Greek phalanx, with its long spears, moved with the armies and the settlers into the plain of the two rivers, becoming the framework of the Hellenistic east for centuries to come. Once the door to the east and to Central Asia stood open, the roads and the embassies linking the Hellenistic world to Parthia, to Bactria and, beyond them, to India were connected into a single system.
result: 安提柯放棄巴比倫，率殘部退往波斯與帕提亞方向，把圍城與攻城器械一併丟在幼發拉底河畔；德美特里的船隊既已折損，也只能退回地中海。塞琉古則進入巴比倫，接收城防、行省稅收與那支象兵，重新被東方承認為亞洲之王。圍城解除的消息傳到安提柯陣營時，他已經退到巴比倫以東數百里的地方，亞歷山大的帝國從此再沒有完整過。這場戰爭的直接勝負並不慘烈：沒有正面會戰的大規模廝殺，勝敗由遠距離的行軍、封鎖與夜襲決定，安提柯在關鍵的一夜損失了全部攻城器械，塞琉古的損失則主要是前312年加薩一戰留下的舊帳。對希臘世界而言，前310年之後巴比倫不再只是亞洲的一個行省，而是一個王國的首都；對兵器而言，這場戰爭也再次說明長矛方陣的極限——它可以守城，可以破營，卻替代不了攻城器械，也無法在沒有水源與糧道的地方撐過冬天。卡面那支斯巴達長矛的形制，在這場戰爭之後仍然是希臘步兵的標準答案，只是它早已讓位給更長的馬其頓薩里沙。
resultEn: Antigonus abandoned Babylon and withdrew with his survivors towards Persia and Parthia, leaving the siege and its engines behind on the banks of the Euphrates; Demetrius's fleet was already broken and could only fall back to the Mediterranean. Seleucus entered Babylon, taking over the defences, the revenues of the satrapy and the elephants, and was recognised once more as king of Asia. When the news that the siege had been lifted reached Antigonus's camp, he was already several hundred miles to the east of the city, and the empire of Alexander was never whole again. The immediate contest was not bloody: there was no great pitched battle, and the outcome was settled by long marches, blockades and a night attack, with Antigonus losing all his siege engines in a single night and Seleucus carrying the old wounds left by Gaza in 312 BC. For the Greek world, after 310 BC Babylon was no longer one satrapy among others but the capital of a kingdom; and for the study of weapons this war showed again the limits of the phalanx, which could hold a wall and break a camp but could not replace siege engines and could not survive a winter where there was no water and no supply road. The shape of the Spartan dory on the card remained the standard answer of the Greek infantry, though by then it had already given way to the longer Macedonian sarissa.
